validity.recommendation: verify LengthKnown -- independent sources cluster around 165 mi, ~3.5% below GEM's 171 mi
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=171.00 mi. Two independent sources report a DIFFERENT figure: the FERC Environmental Assessment for docket CP17-19 states 'The intrastate Valley Crossing System consists of approximately 165 miles of 48-inch- and 42-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline' (plus a separate ~1,000-foot / 0.19-mile FERC-jurisdictional border-crossing segment, bringing the FERC-described total to ~165.2 mi); and the Houston Chronicle, reporting directly off Enbridge's own FERC in-service filing, independently states 'The 165-mile pipeline...' A third figure, 168 miles, appears in general web-search summaries attributed to Enbridge's own project descriptions. None of the three sources matches GEM's 171 mi exactly, though all three are within the same ballpark (165-171 mi, a <=3.6% spread) -- plausibly attributable to different measurement endpoints (mainline only vs. mainline + laterals/interconnects) rather than a wrong pipeline. Flagging as a spec question rather than a confident correction: confirm whether 171 mi reflects a later as-built or looped total, or should be revised toward the 165 mi figure both FERC and an independent newspaper (sourced from Enbridge's own regulatory filing) agree on.

validity.recommendation: verify ConstructionYear -- FERC's own EA dates the start of construction to April 2017, not 2018
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records ConstructionYear=2018. The FERC Environmental Assessment for CP17-19 (dated 2017/2018) states plainly: 'Work began on this project in April 2017 and the project is expected to go into service in October 2018.' This is consistent with the wider public record: the Railroad Commission of Texas issued Valley Crossing an intrastate construction permit on Sept 15, 2016, and Enbridge/Spectra began laying pipe on the bulk (non-FERC-jurisdictional) system under that state permit well before the Oct 23, 2017 federal Presidential Permit/NGA authorization for the short border-crossing segment -- a sequence documented contemporaneously (Sierra Club's July 2018 blog post 'Valley Crossing Pipeline: An Exercise in Corporate Trickery' specifically criticizes Enbridge for beginning construction under the state permit before the federal review concluded). A plausible reconciliation: GEM's 2018 may track the FERC-authorized border-crossing segment's own construction start (that piece could not lawfully begin until after the Oct 2017 federal authorization, and a subsequent FERC order approving construction on the jurisdictional facilities is dated ~March 2018) rather than the intrastate system's April 2017 start. Flagging as a spec question since the two plausible readings of 'ConstructionYear' for this hybrid intrastate/interstate project point to different years -- worth a deliberate call on which milestone GEM's field is meant to capture, not treated as a silent pass.
